title: Filter SQLite rows by time components
goal: Filter stored TimeOnly values by hour, minute or second inside SQLite; use translated EF11 predicates or retain parameterized server-side SQL on EF10.

runtime.name: .NET
runtime.reason: EF Core 11 requires .NET11; direct Microsoft.Data.Sqlite11 net10 assets do not establish an EF11-on-net10 route.

sdk.name: .NET SDK
sdk.reason: Build the net11 consumer. Exact RC2 SDK and reference/runtime artifacts are verification pins, not GA evidence.

language.name: C#
language.reason: Current sample language mode; no new C#15 syntax is required by component translation.

frameworks: Microsoft.NET.Sdk console application; no ASP.NET Core framework required

packages.name: Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Sqlite
packages.reason: Use the matching EF11 SQLite provider graph that translates TimeOnly Hour, Minute and Second; RC2 is the exact tested graph.

packageAssets: Current EF/Core/Relational/Sqlite.Core lib/net11.0; Abstractions and Microsoft.Data.Sqlite.Core lib/net10.0. Previous EF10 uses lib/net10.0 and Data.Sqlite.Core lib/net8.0.
Locked actual graphs: EF10.0.13 versus EF11.0.0-rc.2.26504.105; sample packages are author-maintained and do not inherit root update permissions.
providers: Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Sqlite with default TimeOnly TEXT storage; real in-memory SQLite, no EF InMemory or mocks

Measured Windows x64 e_sqlite3: SQLite3.53.3 via SQLitePCLRaw bundle/core/lib/provider2.1.13; SQLite3.53.4 via SQLitePCLRaw bundle/config/core/provider3.0.5 plus SQLite3.53.4. Normal provider bundle initializes native access.
platforms: Executed on Windows x64 with the packaged e_sqlite3 native library. Other OS/architectures require matching native assets and separate validation; not executed here.
renderingModes: Not applicable: console/database queries; no browser rendering
constraints: Default EF TimeOnly nullable TEXT mapping only: no custom converter, REAL day representation or arbitrary legacy text format.
Whole Hour/Minute/Second components only; not timezone conversion, date bucketing, millisecond/microsecond extraction or a universal precision guarantee.
Apply filters before materialization. A server expression can still scan rows in SQLite; no index-use or performance promise.
The EF10 comparison retains parameterized server-side SQL, not a client-evaluation workaround or a ninth .NET10 foundation.
prerequisites: Copy each release into its own standalone directory with all canonical files; acquire the SDK/runtime and locked packages before offline execution.
Use an isolated connection kept open until all contexts/readers are disposed. This sample uses only a disposable in-memory database, with no account, credentials or production data.
Choose the documented standard provider bundle. Replacing retired native bundles, encrypted/custom engines and native initialization alternatives are separate guidance.
stabilityLimitations: These APIs are not publisher-designated experimental; no diagnostic suppression or experimental opt-in. Evidence uses .NET11 RC2, not actual GA. PIN-965 retains GA reconciliation.

evidence.scope: Actual SQLite native version/source ID/DLL hash; eleven exact stored TEXT/null boundary and fractional inputs; tick round-trip; seven executed parameter-safe server filters with exact IDs and strftime SQL. EF10 rejects all three direct component predicates before any command; supported FromSqlInterpolated alternative executes.

humanProof.scope: Automated real SQLite execution covers the bounded stored-value, translation, result and failure controls. Other native platforms/providers, arbitrary storage formats and actual GA remain unverified.
